top.title: US military cloud platform reportedly hacked as Pentagon insists systems are secure
top.description: Hackers reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform late Friday, potentially exposing sensitive military data. The Pentagon did not specifically deny that the system had been accessed, but insists its networks remain secure amid an ongoing spate of cyber-related data incidents.

top.title: Why Pearl-Cohn's return to TSSAA football state championship was never in doubt
top.description: LEXINGTON — The thought crossed Marshall commit Lance Donaldson' s mind that his Pearl-Cohn football career could be over. With two weeks left in the regular season, the Firebirds' leading rusher suffered an ankle injury against White House on Oct. 23 , forcing him to miss the final week of the regular season and potentially more. He said the injury was "a blessing in disguise," letting him add an extra element to his game and be a better player for his team. Donaldson logged 54 yards and two touchdowns on 13 carries giving Pearl-Cohn an edge in a 42-16 victory against Lexington (13-1) in TSSAA football playoff semifinals , in Class 4A on Nov. 27. More TSSAA football championship game pairings for 2026 BlueCross Bowl matchups The win pushes Pearl-Cohn (11-3) back into the 4A state championship game where it will face Alcoa (14-0) at 10 a.m. CT on Dec. 5 at Finley Stadium in Chattanooga. Its the second straight trip to the BlueCross Bowl for Pearl-Cohn and the program's eighth overall championship appearance, having won titles in 1996, 1997 and 2023. "He's (Donaldson) been playing lights out on both sides of the ball," said Pearl-Cohn coach Tony Brunetti, who will coach in his sixth title game on Dec. 5. "That's why he's such a powerful kid and is signing with Marshall next week." Part of Donaldson's deep dive into his game was getting to know those around him. He wanted to get closer to his linemen, not just as teammates, but really understanding the details of what they were doing in front of him. "I feel like my game has gotten better (since the injury)," Donaldson said. "I was able to look at my game from a mental standpoint and look at the things I could do better. Now, I'm able to attack those points and strengthen the ones I'm already good at. Since returning from injury, Donaldson has contributed six touchdowns in four games. Prior to that, he had just four scores in nine games. "He (Donaldson) does everything the right way," Brunetti said. "You don't see him talking or anything. He's a hard-nosed player. He's even lifting weights before the game. Donaldson is hoping for a full-circle moment against Alcoa in Chattanooga . Like many Pearl-Cohn seniors, his career started off with a state championship in 2023 . He wants to leave the same way he came in. His Firebirds took care of business, handing Lexington (13-1) its only loss this season. It'll be a tall task for Pearl-Cohn as Alcoa has won 11 consecutive state titles. "It's great to get one coming in and to get another going out is going to be an amazing feeling," Donaldson said. top.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 26: Timur Tutierov of Sunderland scores his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Sunderland AFC and Jagiellonia Bialystok at Stadium of Light on November 26, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) | Getty Images The searchlight casting its beam into the cold winter’s night, the fireworks, the anthem, the opposition from a far-flung corner of the continent – European football on Wearside, how incredible is that? Yes, I remain excited and enthralled by the whole experience. I think this new format for the three competitions is very cleverly designed; it maintains interest, and the idealist in me is glad that there is such a breadth of clubs and communities coming together, united in football. And then reality hits – or does it? What exactly is that reality? It is very easy to criticise the manager and the players when things don’t go the way we hoped for. Yet these are essentially the same people who got us into this incredible position in the first place. We do need to try to keep a sense of perspective on all of this, not get sucked into some reactionary doom spiral and work out positive ways forward. Let’s consider some of the feelings and concerns that are at the forefront of Sunderland supporters’ minds. When Régis Le Bris was appointed, there seemed to be a coming together of like-minded people at the helm of the club, and there was talk of a long-term plan and “the project”. In my time as a Sunderland supporter, that is pretty revolutionary talk, yet eminently sensible. Over my lifetime, North-East football has been beset by short-termism, constant changes of manager and boardroom personnel, perhaps with the exception (to a degree) of Middlesbrough and Steve Gibson. The plan was clearly for Sunderland to return to the top table and establish themselves in the Premier League. That return probably happened sooner than expected, and what followed last season definitely went way beyond expectations. So the club is possibly still playing catch-up, trying to cope with the significant extra demands at an earlier stage than they hoped for. Recruitment did not go as planned over the summer, and injuries to key players have compounded problems, yet it is important to stick to financial probity and keep working to build a sustainable football club. The players I watch on the pitch are good enough to stay in this league as long as they commit to the cause as they did against Chelsea and Villa. top.title: Sunderland’s Defensive Fragility: Why Are We Making So Many Mistakes?
top.description: Sunderland of 2025/26 was a stubborn unit and one which was an absolute pain in the arse to play against. More importantly, we were a tight defensive unit which defended en masse and backed ourselves against any forwards in the league. The most important thing of all was that we didn’t make many individual mistakes at all. This season, although the back-to-back clean sheets against Chelsea and Villa are an improvement, it feels as though every single goal we concede comes from an error from one of our players who looked so strong last year. The latest in this was Reinildo’s mistake, leading to Jagiellonia Białystok being gifted their equaliser on Thursday night. It was the latest in a series of worrying, schoolboy errors; the Coventry game was full of them, as was the trip to Bournemouth – take your pick. There haven’t been many goals we’ve conceded this year where the opposition have taken us apart. It doesn’t feel like we’re getting outplayed; it feels like we are just letting opponents dominate the ball and giving them chance after chance to keep on. The issue is that we sit back and have this obsession with passing the ball backwards, and on too many occasions we invite pressure onto ourselves. When confidence is rock bottom, this is asking for trouble, and this constant need to pass back and turn down chances to drive forward with the ball – which was successful last season – is proving to be a recipe for disaster. Defenders don’t look comfortable on the ball, and too many of our forwards don’t seem keen to be on the ball on the few occasions we get it to them. All of this combines to make for a team that, in terms of confidence, is a shell of what it was last year. The frustration is that we have a lot of senior defenders who have combined hundreds of appearances under their belts. Reinildo and Omar Alderete have almost 600 appearances between them; they are two of the players who made us so successful defensively last season. Yet this season, they’ve looked like completely different players, although I’ll say Alderete has struggled a lot more than Reinildo, and his early exit on Thursday after a ropey performance sums up his season. We are missing the spine of our team; this goes without saying. Dan Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey are three key figures any club would miss. Having them back sooner rather than later will make a huge difference to our fortunes. top.title: Sunderland’s European Frustration: This Simply Isn’t Good Enough
top.description: I should prefix this by saying it refers to the Europa League only. The Premier League is different, but has its own set of issues. Two problems persist at Sunderland right now. One was quite predictable, but the other gets the blood pressure up to dangerous levels. We are told with regularity that the Premier League takes priority. Now, I don’t know about anyone else, but when I thought of the prospect of playing Europe’s leading lights (no offence to Jagiellonia, but that didn’t include them), I quite honestly thought the Premier League campaign could go and stick its head up a dead bear’s bum. In fairness, that was me forgetting to factor in the chance we might spend a large part of the group stage in the relegation zone. Clearly, that has affected priorities. And I understand that, to an extent. By God, was it evident on Thursday night that the side selected would largely rather not have been there. It was a timid performance that wouldn’t have looked out of place in League One. To emphasise the point, the opposition striker (loosely put) scored one goal in 24 Championship appearances for Oxford last season. He was, by way of review from an Oxford-supporting pal of mine, “shite.” And yet, despite the limitations of our opponent, there was so much phoning it in, you’d think our lads were part of a live telethon to raise funds for a new attacking coach. Which brings me to the big question: what the hell are we doing in training all week, so that the end result is an utter lack of thrust, threat and attacking invention? Why is it that there are no partnerships across the pitch? The players should be far more connected than they are, but they look inert; coached to the point that they have no idea what to do, apart from admiring the opposition in front of us. Or perhaps undercoached, producing a similar effect. Yes, Jagiellonia had lovely shirts, but lads, there’s a football match to be played here. We haven’t all turned up at the game because we want to get away from our families, or because we like sitting in traffic on Wessington Way. It’s because we want to see our club in a competition we’ve dreamed of for years, if not decades. And now it’s here, I’m watching some of the lads play like a dropped PlayStation controller. top.title: OTD (28/11/1998): Gavin McCann Makes His Debut For Sunderland
top.description: Gavin Peter McCann was brought to the club by Peter Reid in 1998 from his old club Everton, for £500,000 – in what turned out to be a very decent piece of business, dropping down a division in the hope of more game time. Arriving in the 1998/99 Division One-winning season (that fantastic 105-point haul), he initially had limited opportunities in what was a very successful Sunderland side. He made his debut, coming on as a substitute, against Sheffield United at Bramall Lane, in a superb 4-0 away victory. But he only really started to settle in his first full season at the club in the FA Carling Premiership, initially in the number 11 shirt (when numbered shirts still meant something!). He was a well-built, strong player, standing just shy of 6ft. Once in the team, he started to become a standout player at the Stadium of Light, with fantastic balance, a great insight and a range of passing ability. He was a strong presence on the pitch, a great tackler, with the ability to get from box to box. Looking back now, in my mind’s eye, for me he resembles the style of a Ray Kennedy (for Liverpool) or a poor man’s Kevin Ball. He got his first full game that December, in a 2-0 home win against Crystal Palace, and in that season’s League Cup semi-final, first leg against Leicester City, he scored his first-ever professional goal, pulling a goal back after we’d gone behind 2-0. We lost 3-2 on aggregate that year. In our memorable campaign back in the Premier League (the first of two seventh-placed finishes), Gavin played 26 times, scoring four and assisting three. There was no hint of second-season syndrome, and McCann was again an integral part of Reid’s team in the 2000/2001 season, getting his first of three goals with a late strike against Arsenal. For me, one of Gavin’s best goals in a Sunderland shirt. The terrier that was Alex Rae robbed Patrick Vieira on the edge of the box, and McCann didn’t hesitate to sweep the ball across the keeper into the far corner of the net to earn a late equaliser. His consistent, powerful performances gained him a call-up to the England squad in February 2001. He came on in the second half in a 3-0 friendly victory against Spain. It was, unfortunately, his only cap. We struggled the following season, and Gavin didn’t register a goal or an assist, but he did play in 29 league matches, the most he’d played in a season for Sunderland. He surpassed that the following season by one match, as we sleepwalked into relegation. Too good for second-tier football, he left for Aston Villa in a £2.25 million deal in July 2003 – a decent-sized profit from when we’d bought him. He spent four seasons at Villa Park before joining Bolton Wanderers in July 2007 for £1 million. He did play in the UEFA Cup whilst there, but sadly had to retire in 2010 due to injury. top.description: I don’t know where the Kentucky Wildcats go from here. They just lost at home to an unranked Wichita State team in overtime, and that may not even have been the worst part. The Cats led by 14 in the first half and lost 73-71 in overtime. At home. On the 50th Anniversary of Rupp Arena’s opening. Kentucky is now 4-3 going into December. Four and three, a far cry from the standard this program once held. Kentucky got out-rebounded 55-36 at home and 23-12 on the offensive glass. That’s unacceptable for any program claiming to be NCAA Tournament-caliber. MVP: Rupp Arena, Big Blue Nation Give the fans credit. A lot of credit. Black Friday night. 9:00 tip. They showed up, trying to will the Cats across the finish line. Against Wichita State. This wasn’t Duke or North Carolina or Louisville or Tennessee. It was Wichita State. Big Blue Nation showed up and were imploring the Cats to finish down the stretch. These fans deserve better. Box Score First Half It was a spirited start for Kentucky Friday night. Franck Kepnang, getting the start for an injured Malachi Moreno, scored the first four points for the Cats, including two on an alley-oop dunk. Kepnang also had an emphatic block just before the media timeout, practically spiking the ball out of bounds. But the Cats’ offensive struggles would continue for the next few minutes. top.title: Texas football's championship-level defense needs help to realize CFP title hopes | Golden
top.description: Texas Longhorns defensive lineman Alex January (97) dives after Texas A&M Aggies wide receiver Mario Craver (1) in the first quarter of the Lone Star Showdown game between Texas and Texas A&M at Kyle Field in College Station, Nov. 27, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) COLLEGE STATION - Georgia isn't quaking in its boots after this one but the Texas Longhorns earned a chance to play their nemesis in what will be an historic showdown for the SEC championship. No one said it this would be easy. OK, I did since had the Longhorns taking down the reeling Texas A&M Aggies by a 31-17 score. Not the first time I've misfired, but the result was what many of us predicted would happen; at least if we're talking about the old moneyline. At this point of the season, the only result that matter is the one that places your team under the "W" or the "L" in the ledger. Texas' 16-6 win came before 109,570 at Kyle Field, including Aggies fans who showed up for meeting No. 121 and an end the most-lost season in many a year. And it was about as ugly as the scored indicated. The Texas offense struggled like it did at LSU. Quarterback Arch Manning locked in on receivers and threw an interception in the end zone that cost the Horns a chance to go up double digits with 11 minutes, 4 seconds remaining, but the defense rode in to save the day, like it has on so many occasions. To his credit, Manning (on an 18-for-34, 143-yard passing night that had mall walkers everywhere appreciating the pedestrian showing) helped clinch the win with a 7-yard scramble that set up Gianni Spetic's 42-yard field goal, putting the Horns comfortably in front. UT finished the regular season at 10-2 - that's a preseason prediction I nailed - but the offensive output we witnessed won't cut in the SEC title game against the two-time defending conference champs. The good news is Steve Sarkisian and his staff have plenty of time to come up with a good game plan for the Dec. 5 matchup in Atlanta. MORE CEDDY: Golden and Bohls tackle college football's biggest storylines Meeting No. 121 will go down as a real mudder, but it's the kind of football that has provided a blueprint to Texas' 2026 success. But for Enzo Maresca’s side it is a necessary step to take on their journey and development. It is time to adjust expectations on this Manchester City to what the reality of their situation is. top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BUFFALO, N.Y. — Go figure. The Pittsburgh Penguins won, and did so with the youth movement leading the way, while a few of the roughest performances were submitted by the most established veterans. The game wasn’t always pretty or even well played. The story of the game was not simply the Penguins gradually improving the quality of team play but specifically, it was those born in the 21st century who were the players to do it. Unmistakably, the first period was achingly bland and uncompetitive for both teams. top.title: Jesper Wallstedt Wants to Play Goal in 70 Games Per Year for Wild
top.description: Jesper Wallstedt Wild Getty Minnesota Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt says that he wants to play goalie in more than 70 games for his team going forward. Wallstedt has been incredible for Minnesota this season, helping the team to the best record in the Western Conference while putting up outstanding individual numbers for the Wild. With Filip Gustavsson finally back from his offseason hip surgery, Wallstedt is expected to get more rest for Minnesota after starting most of the team’s games in the first two months of the season. But if it were up to him, he would start in over 70 games per season. Jesper Wallstedt Wants to Shoulder Heavy Load for Wild Speaking to Joe Smith of The Athletic , Wallstedt would like to follow in the footsteps of his idol, New York Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist, who played goal in 70+ games for four straight seasons for NY. “Honestly, I think so. If you want your goalie to play, he can play. I’ve seen this narrative of a lot of media saying that goalies burn out or they get tired before the playoffs. I’ve never seen a goalie say that they’re burned out. … Obviously, it’s a result-based business, so if you don’t succeed, there’s stuff like that that is going to come up from outside noise and outside sources. But I’ve never seen a goalie himself say that he was too tired to play. I get back-to-back (resting one game). That makes sense. Especially for the injury purpose of it. But I think if you adapt practice and you adapt morning skates and there’s days off to be had, I think you can play 65 to 70,” Wallstedt said. Play for Filip Gustavsson is Fluid According to Wild head coach John Hynes, the plan for Gustavsson’s playing time is fluid right now, given he just came back from a layoff. “Not even performance, but physical and performance and getting up to speed on the day, the grind of the NHL. We don’t have a set plan yet for it, because it’s a little bit where you want to make sure we’re doing the right things with him and not just throwing him back in there when he might need a little recovery time. Or, maybe he feels great, and he’s playing great, and that might change our opinion as well,” Hynes said. Either way, it’s a good problem for Minnesota to have, as they have two quality goalies. Five points on 2 of 9 at Atlanta Nov. 22, his worst scoring night of the season, then a late scratch at Orlando,” he further added. “The team has not said which tendon. The card shows the two that take the most load in hoops, just above and below the kneecap. Both act as the spring for every jump, landing, and hard stop. Tendon pain climbs with how much spring you ask of it.” “ROAD TO WEDNESDAY VS MEMPHIS: 1. Sunday and Monday: calm it down. Sit the back-to-back, cut the jumping, keep the quad strong with slow heavy work. 2. Tuesday: full speed work. Sprint, cut, jump, land. 3. To play: a knee that feels the same the morning after as the morning before.” “In the NBA’s own injury records from 2016 to 2019, 64% of 138 patellar tendinopathy cases cost no games. When one did, half missed 2 games or fewer, and the longest ran 30. Cade has missed 3 of his last 5, so he already sits on the longer side. If Tuesday’s work leaves the knee sore the next morning, I move to Dec 13 at Indiana,” he concluded . The Pistons will likely take a cautious approach with Cade Cunningham, especially with the season still in its early stages. Missing two more games would be a setback, but avoiding a recurring knee issue is more important. He was going to be there for Wrestlepalooza, and we had made plans to catch up at a pre-party before the show. Haley was born and raised in Adelaide, South Australia, and fell in love with professional wrestling at an early age. He spent more than a decade on the Australian independent circuit as Jonah Rock and J-Rock before signing with NXT, WWE's developmental brand, in 2019. He won the NXT North American Championship in 2021, made his main-roster debut in 2022 and won the André the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in 2024, a year after finishing as the runner-up. He was in the middle of a main-event feud with Oba Femi. His last appearance was at Crown Jewel on Nov. 7. Those are the things that will lead the tributes, and they should. But that's not who I think of when I hear his name. I spent two years with WWE, and part of that job meant regular trips to the WWE Performance Center in Orlando to work with NXT. I was a sportswriter who had spent most of my career in press boxes and locker rooms, now trying to find my footing on camera in a world I had loved as a fan but never quite fit into. The Performance Center can be an intimidating place for someone like that. It's full of people who have trained their entire lives for that moment. Jermaine was one of the first people who made it feel smaller. He was a sneaker head, and when he found out I had covered the NBA for most of my career, that was it. He wanted to know everything. Critics warn that heavy reliance on AI weakens critical thinking, creativity, and human mentorship in education while widening the digital divide. nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure For Mrs Usman, the day started like any other school day. Her husband went to pick up their two children from Oakland Kids Nursery and Primary School, Oda Road, Akure, not knowing that their little daughter would come home with a story that would change their family forever. It was at home that evening that the truth began to unfold. Their 3-year-old daughter, a KG II pupil, quietly told her elder brother, who is in Nursery II, that a boy in her class had touched her. How father heard Her father overheard the conversation. Worried, he called the little girl and asked her to explain. She mentioned the name of her classmate and said he touched her private part. Her father immediately called her mother. At first, Mrs. Usman thought it might be a child’s misunderstanding. But when she got home after 7pm, she checked her daughter’s pants and saw blood stains. And when the child urinated, she cried out in pain. Asked again who touched her, she repeated the same name. Asked why she did not tell her teachers, the little girl said she was afraid she would be beaten. Nightmare, search for healthcare That night, the family rushed to a nearby pharmacy. The pharmacists said they could not handle such a case and advised them to see a paediatrician. The next day, October 28, Mrs. Usman took her daughter to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Akure. After examination, doctors confirmed the child had been defiled. With the medical report in hand, she went straight to the school to report. ‘CCTV not working’ According to her, the proprietor expressed shock. But when she asked to see the CCTV footage of the classroom, she was told the camera was not working. She also asked that the parents of the boy be informed. She said the school did not do so until the following day, after she raised her voice. The boy’s mother, on hearing the news, was said to have queried the school for not informing her earlier. Mother’s cry Mrs. Usman said she only asked for one thing: that her daughter should not remain in the same class as the boy. Instead, she said the proprietor suggested moving her daughter to Nursery I, where she would repeat the class if she could not cope. “Why should my daughter, the victim, be the one to be moved?” she asked. nigeria.description: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday. Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida. The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup. For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested. Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio. German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar. The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012. nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi The sound of gunfire shattered the campaign atmosphere at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, November 23. People who had gathered for a political rally suddenly scrambled for safety. Women ran, campaigners scattered and, in the ensuing chaos, bullets found human targets. By the time the shooting stopped, families had lost loved ones, several people critically wounded and communities plunged into mourning. Among the disturbing details was that six truckloads of policemen had reportedly been deployed to provide security. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, put their number at close to 50. Yet, according to accounts from both political camps, the violence escalated despite the robust security presence. The tragedy has since generated competing accusations between the All Progressives Congress, APC, and the National Democratic Congress, NDC. Beneath the political blame game are grieving families, wounded survivors and ordinary citizens asking why a political gathering should become a death trap. A Trail Of Troubled Political Gatherings Uduere was not an isolated incident in the build-up to Delta 2027 elections. September 18, a one-million-man march organised by the NDC in the Warri-Effurun axis was disrupted by violence, leaving persons wounded. An AK-47 allegedly recovered from a suspect identified as Collins became a subject of controversy between the party and police. The NDC alleged the suspect was released the following day, a claim that formed part of its subsequent complaints about police handling of the incident. October 3, the party held a 10,000-man march against hunger in Ughelli. The following day, the Ughelli North Local Government Council, chaired by Chief Jaro Egbo, issued a notice, sealed the business premises and impounded truck belonging to Tobore Alex Agbah, who led the march. Agbah would later become one of the victims of the Uduere violence. November 7, another NDC one-million-man march in Asaba ended in violence, with one fatality recorded. The recurrence of disturbances has fuelled allegations that NDC gatherings are being targeted by political opponents allegedly linked to the ruling APC. Delta State Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, however, rejected the suggestion of a pattern. “It’s not a pattern, because when you talk about a pattern, it means that it’s continuously and then you are linking it to be able to join one to the other,” he said. He argued: “The NDC is not being attacked, there are a number of local governments where we have not had any disturbances. nigeria.title: INEC tests BVAS, result portal today
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. The list gives the state, local government area, ward, polling unit and delimitation code of each selected location. It runs alphabetically from Abia State to Zamfara State, with the FCT last. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. Forest made a flying start to the encounter, taking the lead just five minutes into the game through Igor Jesus, who produced a superb volley from Daniel Muñoz’s cross to put the hosts ahead. Chelsea struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Forest looking more dangerous and organised in attack. Despite enjoying more possession, the visitors failed to turn their dominance on the ball into meaningful goalscoring opportunities. The hosts doubled their advantage shortly after the restart when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot in the 51st minute. The penalty was awarded after Wesley Fofana brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea box. However, Chelsea responded three minutes later through substitute Emmanuel Emegha, who pulled one back after Pedro Neto’s effort took a deflection and fell kindly into his path. The goal briefly offered Chelsea hope of mounting a comeback, but Forest remained dangerous and restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute when Gibbs-White grabbed his second of the evening. Chelsea refused to surrender, with Emegha scoring again in the 89th minute to reduce the deficit to 3-2 and set up a tense finish. However, Forest held on through the closing moments to secure all three points and condemn Chelsea to another painful defeat. The result represents another setback for Alonso, whose team have struggled for consistency in recent weeks. Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses and inability to control crucial moments once again proved costly. For Nottingham Forest, the victory provides a significant boost and a valuable reward for their determination and attacking efficiency. Chelsea must now turn their attention to their next Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace as they look to recover from another frustrating night. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. That pushed November outflows to about $5.39 billion, extending what was already a record month for the funds. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. sports.title: Why Pearl-Cohn's return to TSSAA football state championship was never in doubt
sports.description: LEXINGTON — The thought crossed Marshall commit Lance Donaldson' s mind that his Pearl-Cohn football career could be over. With two weeks left in the regular season, the Firebirds' leading rusher suffered an ankle injury against White House on Oct. 23 , forcing him to miss the final week of the regular season and potentially more. He said the injury was "a blessing in disguise," letting him add an extra element to his game and be a better player for his team. Donaldson logged 54 yards and two touchdowns on 13 carries giving Pearl-Cohn an edge in a 42-16 victory against Lexington (13-1) in TSSAA football playoff semifinals , in Class 4A on Nov. 27. More TSSAA football championship game pairings for 2026 BlueCross Bowl matchups The win pushes Pearl-Cohn (11-3) back into the 4A state championship game where it will face Alcoa (14-0) at 10 a.m. CT on Dec. 5 at Finley Stadium in Chattanooga. Its the second straight trip to the BlueCross Bowl for Pearl-Cohn and the program's eighth overall championship appearance, having won titles in 1996, 1997 and 2023. "He's (Donaldson) been playing lights out on both sides of the ball," said Pearl-Cohn coach Tony Brunetti, who will coach in his sixth title game on Dec. 5. "That's why he's such a powerful kid and is signing with Marshall next week." Part of Donaldson's deep dive into his game was getting to know those around him. He wanted to get closer to his linemen, not just as teammates, but really understanding the details of what they were doing in front of him. "I feel like my game has gotten better (since the injury)," Donaldson said. "I was able to look at my game from a mental standpoint and look at the things I could do better. Now, I'm able to attack those points and strengthen the ones I'm already good at. Since returning from injury, Donaldson has contributed six touchdowns in four games. Prior to that, he had just four scores in nine games. "He (Donaldson) does everything the right way," Brunetti said. "You don't see him talking or anything. He's a hard-nosed player. He's even lifting weights before the game. Donaldson is hoping for a full-circle moment against Alcoa in Chattanooga . Like many Pearl-Cohn seniors, his career started off with a state championship in 2023 . He wants to leave the same way he came in. His Firebirds took care of business, handing Lexington (13-1) its only loss this season. It'll be a tall task for Pearl-Cohn as Alcoa has won 11 consecutive state titles. "It's great to get one coming in and to get another going out is going to be an amazing feeling," Donaldson said. sports.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 26: Timur Tutierov of Sunderland scores his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Sunderland AFC and Jagiellonia Bialystok at Stadium of Light on November 26, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) | Getty Images The searchlight casting its beam into the cold winter’s night, the fireworks, the anthem, the opposition from a far-flung corner of the continent – European football on Wearside, how incredible is that? Yes, I remain excited and enthralled by the whole experience. I think this new format for the three competitions is very cleverly designed; it maintains interest, and the idealist in me is glad that there is such a breadth of clubs and communities coming together, united in football. And then reality hits – or does it? What exactly is that reality? It is very easy to criticise the manager and the players when things don’t go the way we hoped for. Yet these are essentially the same people who got us into this incredible position in the first place. We do need to try to keep a sense of perspective on all of this, not get sucked into some reactionary doom spiral and work out positive ways forward. Let’s consider some of the feelings and concerns that are at the forefront of Sunderland supporters’ minds. When Régis Le Bris was appointed, there seemed to be a coming together of like-minded people at the helm of the club, and there was talk of a long-term plan and “the project”. In my time as a Sunderland supporter, that is pretty revolutionary talk, yet eminently sensible. Over my lifetime, North-East football has been beset by short-termism, constant changes of manager and boardroom personnel, perhaps with the exception (to a degree) of Middlesbrough and Steve Gibson. The plan was clearly for Sunderland to return to the top table and establish themselves in the Premier League. That return probably happened sooner than expected, and what followed last season definitely went way beyond expectations. So the club is possibly still playing catch-up, trying to cope with the significant extra demands at an earlier stage than they hoped for. sports.title: Sunderland’s Defensive Fragility: Why Are We Making So Many Mistakes?
sports.description: Sunderland of 2025/26 was a stubborn unit and one which was an absolute pain in the arse to play against. More importantly, we were a tight defensive unit which defended en masse and backed ourselves against any forwards in the league. The most important thing of all was that we didn’t make many individual mistakes at all. This season, although the back-to-back clean sheets against Chelsea and Villa are an improvement, it feels as though every single goal we concede comes from an error from one of our players who looked so strong last year. The latest in this was Reinildo’s mistake, leading to Jagiellonia Białystok being gifted their equaliser on Thursday night. It was the latest in a series of worrying, schoolboy errors; the Coventry game was full of them, as was the trip to Bournemouth – take your pick. There haven’t been many goals we’ve conceded this year where the opposition have taken us apart. It doesn’t feel like we’re getting outplayed; it feels like we are just letting opponents dominate the ball and giving them chance after chance to keep on. The issue is that we sit back and have this obsession with passing the ball backwards, and on too many occasions we invite pressure onto ourselves. When confidence is rock bottom, this is asking for trouble, and this constant need to pass back and turn down chances to drive forward with the ball – which was successful last season – is proving to be a recipe for disaster. Defenders don’t look comfortable on the ball, and too many of our forwards don’t seem keen to be on the ball on the few occasions we get it to them. All of this combines to make for a team that, in terms of confidence, is a shell of what it was last year. The frustration is that we have a lot of senior defenders who have combined hundreds of appearances under their belts. Reinildo and Omar Alderete have almost 600 appearances between them; they are two of the players who made us so successful defensively last season. Yet this season, they’ve looked like completely different players, although I’ll say Alderete has struggled a lot more than Reinildo, and his early exit on Thursday after a ropey performance sums up his season. We are missing the spine of our team; this goes without saying. Dan Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey are three key figures any club would miss. sports.title: Sunderland’s European Frustration: This Simply Isn’t Good Enough
sports.description: I should prefix this by saying it refers to the Europa League only. The Premier League is different, but has its own set of issues. Two problems persist at Sunderland right now. One was quite predictable, but the other gets the blood pressure up to dangerous levels. We are told with regularity that the Premier League takes priority. Now, I don’t know about anyone else, but when I thought of the prospect of playing Europe’s leading lights (no offence to Jagiellonia, but that didn’t include them), I quite honestly thought the Premier League campaign could go and stick its head up a dead bear’s bum. In fairness, that was me forgetting to factor in the chance we might spend a large part of the group stage in the relegation zone. Clearly, that has affected priorities. And I understand that, to an extent. By God, was it evident on Thursday night that the side selected would largely rather not have been there. It was a timid performance that wouldn’t have looked out of place in League One. To emphasise the point, the opposition striker (loosely put) scored one goal in 24 Championship appearances for Oxford last season. He was, by way of review from an Oxford-supporting pal of mine, “shite.” And yet, despite the limitations of our opponent, there was so much phoning it in, you’d think our lads were part of a live telethon to raise funds for a new attacking coach. Which brings me to the big question: what the hell are we doing in training all week, so that the end result is an utter lack of thrust, threat and attacking invention? Why is it that there are no partnerships across the pitch? The players should be far more connected than they are, but they look inert; coached to the point that they have no idea what to do, apart from admiring the opposition in front of us. Or perhaps undercoached, producing a similar effect. Yes, Jagiellonia had lovely shirts, but lads, there’s a football match to be played here. We haven’t all turned up at the game because we want to get away from our families, or because we like sitting in traffic on Wessington Way. It’s because we want to see our club in a competition we’ve dreamed of for years, if not decades. And now it’s here, I’m watching some of the lads play like a dropped PlayStation controller. sports.title: OTD (28/11/1998): Gavin McCann Makes His Debut For Sunderland
sports.description: Gavin Peter McCann was brought to the club by Peter Reid in 1998 from his old club Everton, for £500,000 – in what turned out to be a very decent piece of business, dropping down a division in the hope of more game time. Arriving in the 1998/99 Division One-winning season (that fantastic 105-point haul), he initially had limited opportunities in what was a very successful Sunderland side. He made his debut, coming on as a substitute, against Sheffield United at Bramall Lane, in a superb 4-0 away victory. But he only really started to settle in his first full season at the club in the FA Carling Premiership, initially in the number 11 shirt (when numbered shirts still meant something!). He was a well-built, strong player, standing just shy of 6ft. Once in the team, he started to become a standout player at the Stadium of Light, with fantastic balance, a great insight and a range of passing ability. He was a strong presence on the pitch, a great tackler, with the ability to get from box to box. Looking back now, in my mind’s eye, for me he resembles the style of a Ray Kennedy (for Liverpool) or a poor man’s Kevin Ball. He got his first full game that December, in a 2-0 home win against Crystal Palace, and in that season’s League Cup semi-final, first leg against Leicester City, he scored his first-ever professional goal, pulling a goal back after we’d gone behind 2-0. We lost 3-2 on aggregate that year. In our memorable campaign back in the Premier League (the first of two seventh-placed finishes), Gavin played 26 times, scoring four and assisting three. There was no hint of second-season syndrome, and McCann was again an integral part of Reid’s team in the 2000/2001 season, getting his first of three goals with a late strike against Arsenal. For me, one of Gavin’s best goals in a Sunderland shirt. The terrier that was Alex Rae robbed Patrick Vieira on the edge of the box, and McCann didn’t hesitate to sweep the ball across the keeper into the far corner of the net to earn a late equaliser. His consistent, powerful performances gained him a call-up to the England squad in February 2001. He came on in the second half in a 3-0 friendly victory against Spain. It was, unfortunately, his only cap. We struggled the following season, and Gavin didn’t register a goal or an assist, but he did play in 29 league matches, the most he’d played in a season for Sunderland. He surpassed that the following season by one match, as we sleepwalked into relegation. Too good for second-tier football, he left for Aston Villa in a £2.25 million deal in July 2003 – a decent-sized profit from when we’d bought him. He spent four seasons at Villa Park before joining Bolton Wanderers in July 2007 for £1 million. He did play in the UEFA Cup whilst there, but sadly had to retire in 2010 due to injury. sports.title: Jesper Wallstedt Wants to Play Goal in 70 Games Per Year for Wild
sports.description: Jesper Wallstedt Wild Getty Minnesota Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt says that he wants to play goalie in more than 70 games for his team going forward. Wallstedt has been incredible for Minnesota this season, helping the team to the best record in the Western Conference while putting up outstanding individual numbers for the Wild. With Filip Gustavsson finally back from his offseason hip surgery, Wallstedt is expected to get more rest for Minnesota after starting most of the team’s games in the first two months of the season. But if it were up to him, he would start in over 70 games per season. Jesper Wallstedt Wants to Shoulder Heavy Load for Wild Speaking to Joe Smith of The Athletic , Wallstedt would like to follow in the footsteps of his idol, New York Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist, who played goal in 70+ games for four straight seasons for NY. “Honestly, I think so. If you want your goalie to play, he can play. I’ve seen this narrative of a lot of media saying that goalies burn out or they get tired before the playoffs. I’ve never seen a goalie say that they’re burned out. … Obviously, it’s a result-based business, so if you don’t succeed, there’s stuff like that that is going to come up from outside noise and outside sources. But I’ve never seen a goalie himself say that he was too tired to play. I get back-to-back (resting one game). That makes sense. Especially for the injury purpose of it. But I think if you adapt practice and you adapt morning skates and there’s days off to be had, I think you can play 65 to 70,” Wallstedt said. Play for Filip Gustavsson is Fluid According to Wild head coach John Hynes, the plan for Gustavsson’s playing time is fluid right now, given he just came back from a layoff. “Not even performance, but physical and performance and getting up to speed on the day, the grind of the NHL. We don’t have a set plan yet for it, because it’s a little bit where you want to make sure we’re doing the right things with him and not just throwing him back in there when he might need a little recovery time. Or, maybe he feels great, and he’s playing great, and that might change our opinion as well,” Hynes said. Either way, it’s a good problem for Minnesota to have, as they have two quality goalies. sports.description: The last text Jermaine Haley sent me was five words long. "See you soon my friend." We were supposed to see each other next month in Perth. He was going to be there for Wrestlepalooza, and we had made plans to catch up at a pre-party before the show. sports.title: Hands off Erling! Maresca insists Haaland is fine despite four-game drought ahead of massive Arsenal test
sports.description: RB Leipzig v Manchester City - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Enzo Maresca has defended Erling Haaland after the striker went four consecutive appearances without a goal following a blistering start of 14 goals in his first 12 games. Following Tuesday's 2-2 draw against Napoli, the Manchester City boss insisted Haaland's mood and on-pitch gestures are normal for a striker. Maresca backs Haaland after four-game dry spell Erling Haaland arrives at the Emirates Stadium on a four-match run without a goal after scoring 14 times in his opening 12 games of the season. After Tuesday's 2-2 draw with Napoli, Haaland admitted City are searching for what is missing and called the trip to Arsenal their hardest match of the campaign so far. Maresca stressed that frustration is natural when results dip, noting that Haaland was dancing on the pitch and in training just a few weeks ago. "Erling is upset. I'm upset because we're not winning games. But this is our job, this is football. That's why I need to maintain the balance," Maresca said. Why Haaland's gestures do not worry City's boss Clips of Haaland gesturing on the pitch have drawn attention during Manchester City's four-game winless run across all competitions. Maresca dismissed concerns that his star striker's body language hurts his performance or reflects dressing-room unrest. "I think he gesticulates when we were winning games, and not receiving balls," Maresca explained. "He's a nine. They live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don't score or win games they're upset. So I don't think that affects his game but for sure he's not happy not winning games but everyone is on the same page." Training standards remain high despite four-game skid While Rayan Cherki and Ayyoub Bouaddi rescued a 2-2 draw against Napoli after City's recent dip, Maresca insisted Haaland has not let his standards slip behind the scenes. "He has been good. Yes, normal like since day one. Again, a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch, he was dancing in training. He's happy," Maresca added. "It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games. But I don't see any problem at all with Erling." Haaland and Cherki rally for high-stakes trip to Arsenal Cherki echoed the urgency around the squad by demanding greater energy and stating that winning in north London is the only objective. With a six-point gap separating Arsenal and third-placed City, Maresca will look to his number nine to rediscover his clinical edge on one of the season's biggest stages.
